_meta.purpose: Curated reference set of common RF signals for sigidwiki-style identification of captured emitters. Used by survey/identify.py to rank candidate IDs against modulation features extracted from Pluto IQ.
_meta.source: Hand-curated from well-established public signal characteristics, modeled on sigidwiki.com (The Signal Identification Guide). This is a STARTER set, NOT a scrape of the full wiki — extend data/sigidwiki_ref.json as you confirm signals in the field.
_meta.url_note: 'url' fields are sigidwiki search links (always resolve); confirm the exact entry by eye/ear against the live page before relying on an ID.
_meta.license_note: sigidwiki content is CC BY-NC-SA. Use for internal identification; do NOT embed their waterfall images in client deliverables without attribution / non-commercial review.

signals.name: Analog FM audio (wireless mic / room bug)
signals.tscm: Classic analog audio bug / body wire / wireless mic. Continuous carrier; confirm by listening (FM demod).

signals.name: Narrowband FM voice (NFM)
signals.tscm: Two-way radio / low-rate analog voice. PTT-gated (bursty) unless a bug.

signals.name: FM broadcast
signals.tscm: Commercial broadcast. Expected ambient; not a threat unless a bug hides on an adjacent channel.

signals.name: Analog video transmitter (2.4/5.8 GHz FPV/bug)
signals.tscm: Covert analog video / FPV link. Wide (~6-18 MHz) continuous FM emission.

signals.name: Wi-Fi 802.11 (2.4 GHz)
signals.tscm: WLAN. Bursty wideband OFDM. A hidden camera/AP often rides Wi-Fi — check the device inventory.

signals.name: Wi-Fi 802.11 (5 GHz U-NII)
signals.tscm: 5 GHz WLAN. Wide OFDM, bursty.

signals.name: Bluetooth / BLE
signals.tscm: Frequency-hopping ~1-2 MHz channels across 2.4 GHz. Many covert audio/track devices use BLE — cross-check inventory.

signals.name: Zigbee / 802.15.4 (2.4 GHz)
signals.tscm: IoT/home-automation mesh. ~2 MHz channels. Could be a sensor or a disguised device.

signals.name: DECT cordless phone
signals.tscm: Cordless phone / some baby monitors & bugs. ~1.728 MHz channels.

signals.name: OOK/ASK remote (keyfob, garage, ISM)
signals.tscm: 315/433/868/915 MHz remotes, sensors, TPMS. Short bursts. A bug may beacon on ISM.

signals.name: FSK telemetry / sensor (ISM)
signals.tscm: Low-rate 2-FSK telemetry on ISM bands — sensors, trackers, some covert data links.

signals.name: POCSAG paging
signals.tscm: Paging. Distinctive 2-FSK bursts; decodable. Expected ambient in many areas.

signals.name: DMR (digital mobile radio)
signals.tscm: Digital two-way radio. 12.5 kHz 4FSK, two-slot TDMA.

signals.name: P25 (public safety)
signals.tscm: Public-safety digital voice. Expected ambient.

signals.name: TETRA
signals.tscm: European public-safety/commercial trunked radio.

signals.name: GSM
signals.tscm: 2G cellular. 200 kHz GMSK. A GSM bug (audio over cellular) can look like ordinary GSM uplink.

signals.name: LTE / 4G
signals.tscm: 4G cellular, 1.4-20 MHz channels. Cellular-based bugs hide in uplink traffic.

signals.name: NOAA weather radio
signals.tscm: Government weather broadcast. Expected ambient.

signals.name: GPS L1 (reference)
signals.tscm: GPS downlink reference. Energy ABOVE the noise floor here is suspect — GPS is normally below it; a strong carrier may be a tracker's GPS jammer/repeater.

signals.name: FHSS spread-spectrum (generic)
signals.tscm: Frequency-hopping link — drone control, some covert audio/data devices. Hard to track; dwell long and watch the band.
